subject: Information Theory
title: Mutation Rates Across Species
description: Learn Mutation Rates Across Species in one minute.

hook.text: Bacteria mutate faster than humans—10⁻⁶ per base versus 10⁻⁸. Speed versus accuracy, different strategies.

buildup.text: Organisms with short generations tolerate higher error rates. Rapid mutation lets them adapt to changing environments.

discovery.text: RNA viruses have the highest rates—10⁻³ to 10⁻⁵ per base. They mutate so fast they exist as swarms of variants.

twist.text: An error threshold exists: if mutation rate exceeds a critical value, information is lost faster than selection saves.

climax.text: Eigen's error catastrophe: above the threshold, the genome dissolves into randomness. Life requires minimum fidelity.

punchline.text: Too few errors: no adaptation. Too many: information collapse.

quiz.question: What is Eigen's error catastrophe?
options: When mutation rate exceeds the threshold and genetic information is lost
